lessons.title: Greetings and French vowels
lessons.objective: Greetings and French vowels: Keep French vowels short and steady, and keep u (tu) and ou (vous) apart.
lessons.explanation:

lessons.title: Le, la, un and une
lessons.objective: Le, la, un and une: A noun has grammatical gender.
lessons.explanation:
A noun has grammatical gender. Learn its article with it: le livre, la table. Un and une mean a or an, and l' hides the gender before a vowel: l'école (f.); gender is not a rule about the object itself.
Il y a une table dans la salle de classe. — There is a table in the classroom.
Le livre est sur la table. — The book is on the table.

lessons.objective: One thing or several: Add a written -s to make a plural; it is silent, so listen to the article: le livre, les livres.

lessons.title: Who is speaking?
lessons.objective: Who is speaking?: Je means I, tu means informal you, and vous means formal you or more than one person.
lessons.explanation:
Je means I, tu means informal you, and vous means formal you or more than one person. French never drops the subject pronoun: je, tu, il, elle, on, nous, vous, ils, elles. Moi and toi add stress, and c'est identifies a person.
Moi, je suis Léa. — I am Léa.
Toi, tu es Hugo. — You are Hugo.

lessons.title: Il y a: what exists
lessons.objective: Il y a: what exists: Il y a means there is or there are.
lessons.explanation:
Il y a means there is or there are. Its form does not change for one or many. Use il y a to introduce something; use être to locate a known thing. After a negative, un, une and des become de or d', and de also replaces des before a plural adjective + noun.
Il y a une bibliothèque à l'école. — There is a library at the school.
Il y a de grandes tables. — There are large tables.

lessons.title: The passé composé with avoir
lessons.objective: The passé composé with avoir: The passé composé reports completed past actions.
lessons.explanation:
The passé composé reports completed past actions. Use avoir plus the past participle: -er → -é, -ir → -i, -re → -u; a few are irregular, such as écrit, fait and lu. The accent on -é marks the past participle: j'étudie (present) but j'ai étudié (past).
Hier, j'ai étudié à la bibliothèque. — Yesterday I studied in the library.
